name: Machining Technology
description: Machining programmes train the people who cut metal to a tolerance — on lathes, mills and grinders, and on the computer-controlled machines that have largely replaced turning handwheels by hand. ⚠ The trade is measured in thousandths, and the part is either in tolerance or it is scrap.
degreesNote: Florida's framework is **Machining Technologies, 1,500 hours across four occupational completion points** — machinist helper, machinist operator, machinist setup operator, machinist — and the ladder inside it is the career: an OPERATOR runs a machine someone else set up, a SETUP operator prepares it, and a MACHINIST decides how the part will be made. ⚠ A separate 12-credit **CNC Machinist/Fabricator** college certificate exists for people adding computer control to existing skills. ⚠⚠ The whole programme is taught at only eleven Florida institutions — a small footprint for a trade this fundamental, and worth checking against where you live before you plan on it.

cips.note: Machine shop technology — the programme itself: **11 Florida public institutions** and 86 credentials in 2023. ⚠ A small footprint for a fundamental trade, and the reason this page tells you to check the school list before planning on it.

Machine tool technology — seven institutions and 20 credentials. ⚠ Included because Florida colleges file essentially the same training under both codes, and a student searching one would miss the other.
Computer numerically controlled machining — one institution, 21 credentials. ⚠ Small, but it is the CNC-specific code and belongs with the rest.

related.note: ⚠ The other half of a fabrication shop, taught at the same colleges: welding joins metal, machining cuts it to size. Holding both is common and makes a technician far more useful in a small shop.
Where machining sits inside a modern plant — automation, controls and the maintenance of the machines themselves. The usual route from running a machine to keeping the line running.
The degree route above the bench: CAD/CAM, manufacturing engineering technology and quality, and the step toward programming and process planning rather than production.
